phase_intent: base for Spark-Hermes-3.8-27B. Trained and scored in bf16 on a 96 GB card; distributed as GGUF sized for a 32 GB card, which is a separate artifact whose scores must be re-measured rather than inherited.
parameters_note: Derived from model.safetensors.index.json: total_size 55562855904 bytes over 18 shards, at 2 bytes per bf16 parameter. Read off the index rather than the model card, because the card rounds to '27B' and the pin is what a memory budget is computed from.
hermes_dialect_evidence:
the repository's own chat_template.jinja wraps each call as <tool_call>
<function=NAME>
<parameter=KEY>
value
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>, returns results in <tool_response>, and renders deliberation from message['reasoning_content'] into a <think> block. It shares Hermes's OUTER tags -- <tool_call> and <think> are both present -- and emits no <atem:function_calls>. But the payload inside <tool_call> is one element per parameter, NOT the Hermes '{"name": ..., "arguments": {...}}' JSON object, so hermes.protocol's JSON decoder finds no call on any turn. This model does not speak Hermes, and it is the tag overlap that makes saying so necessary: the dialect cannot be established by looking for <tool_call>. Established by reading the pinned template; see docs/serving-qwen3.8.md for what has and has not been confirmed by generation.
dialect_note: The pinned artifact for this dialect is upstream's own chat_template.jinja, committed at hermes/templates/chat-template-qwen35.jinja, and hermes.conformance checks that every marker hermes/qwen35.py parses is still present in it. There is no rendered system prompt to pin because this repo writes no tool block for QWEN35: the definitions go with the request so the template renders its own '# Tools' system turn, the <tools> array and the call-format instruction as one consistent block. Writing our own alongside it would condition the model on two tool blocks in the same prompt.
serving: NOT YET ESTABLISHED in this repo. The published config declares transformers_version 5.8.0.dev0 and the tags advertise vLLM and SGLang compatibility, but neither has been run against this pin here, and the previous base needed SGLang built from a branch after eight startup failures. scripts/serve_agent.sh carries the recipe it had for Muse-Glimmer and has NOT been re-verified for this architecture. Treat a first bring-up as unproven work, not as a config change.
text_config_note: Every text hyperparameter is nested under text_config. This is a Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, so the top level of config.json carries only vision and projector keys -- anything reading it for hidden_size or num_hidden_layers gets None and computes a memory budget out of nothing. tests/test_base_model.py asserts the nesting for that reason. AutoModelForCausalLM also refuses this config outright; the class is AutoModelForImageTextToText. Three base models in a row have had this shape.
kv_bytes_per_token_note: Over the 16 FULL-ATTENTION layers only: 2 * 16 * 4 kv_heads * 256 head_dim * 2 bytes. This model is hybrid -- layer_types is 48 linear_attention + 16 full_attention, one full-attention layer every full_attention_interval (4) -- and the 48 linear layers hold a fixed-size recurrent state per SEQUENCE rather than a per-token cache, so they belong in a bounded per-sequence budget and not in a figure multiplied by a context length. Counting all 64 layers would give 262144 and overstate the per-token cost by 4x, which is how a card that runs this model comfortably gets ruled out on paper.
kv_bytes_measured_note: NULL DELIBERATELY. The figures above are derived from config.json arithmetic and have NOT been confirmed against a live server for this base. The previous pin carried a measurement -- 7.52 GiB over 606,251 tokens on SGLang against Muse-Glimmer-30B -- and those numbers describe a different model with a different layer count, KV-head count and head_dim; carrying them across would assert evidence that does not exist here, and stale and fresh look identical once written down. This is the field that caught a 4x error last time, and it only caught it because a real server contradicted the derivation. Until someone serves this pin and reads SGLang's own KV pool printout, the derivation is unconfirmed and this stays null.
context_note: max_position_embeddings is 262144 natively; the model card describes extension to ~1M. A budget saying input_tokens: 262144 without saying whether that is cumulative or PEAK context cannot be checked against a card at all -- the two readings differ by more than an order of magnitude. kv_bytes() takes a peak context. At fp8 and a 262,144-token peak, the derived figure is ~8.6 GB.
